_comment: The EAGER GRAPH's gzip ceiling, in BYTES. This file is the single source of
truth: it used to be prose in a docs/BACKLOG.md row, raised and recorded by
the same person, with no mechanical check in either direction. It was raised
twice in two PRs before anyone could notice.
MEASURE THE SHIPPING BUILD. The bundle must be built with VITE_API_LIVE=true
(what infra/docker/Dockerfile.api sets). A build without it is ~860 B LARGER
and is not what ships -- that discrepancy already made one reviewer report a
wrong figure. scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs builds that variant itself rather
than trusting whatever happens to be in dist/. (It does not 'assert the mode'
-- an earlier version tried to detect the mode from the built output and
silently never fired, because Vite constant-folds VITE_API_LIVE away.)
Raising this number is a deliberate act: say why in the PR body, and expect to
justify it, which is the whole point of it living somewhere a diff can see.
WHAT IS COUNTED (#323): the eager module graph as declared by VITE'S OWN BUILD
MANIFEST (dist/.vite/manifest.json) -- the entry chunk plus the transitive
closure of its static `imports`. `dynamicImports` are excluded, which is
exactly the eager/lazy split.
Two earlier forms of this measurement were both wrong, in the same direction:
1. 'the largest dist/assets/index-*.js'. With manualChunks configured it
measured 19,594 B against a real eager graph of 65,284 B -- a 45,690 B
under-report, reporting headroom that did not exist.
2. 'the entry <script type=module> plus every <link rel=modulepreload> in
dist/index.html'. Correct for form 1's case, but with
build.modulePreload:false Vite emits NO preload links, so a statically
imported 45.69 kB vendor chunk vanished again. Preload links are a HINT;
the manifest is the build's own statement of the graph.
NOT counted, deliberately: CSS (a separate ~8.9 kB gzip that no version of
this gate has ever included), and lazily-imported chunks.
The KEY NAME below is load-bearing. Mistyping or renaming it used to make the
gate read `undefined`, compare `gz > undefined` (false), and print
'bundle budget OK ... headroom NaN B' for a bundle of any size, exit 0. It is
now validated as a positive integer and a bad value FAILS the build.
